name: ActiveMQ
tagline: An ActiveMQ Classic broker over OpenWire, with transactions, durable subscriptions, selectors, the scheduler and dead letters.
point: The users you set; with none, any user and password

capabilities.title: Every message, with its state
capabilities.text: Scheduled, pending, delivered, acked, dead_letter, expired, rolled_back or discarded, with the redelivery count.

capabilities.title: Local and XA transactions
capabilities.text: Sends stay invisible until commit; rollback redelivers. XA prepare, two-phase commit and recover from any connection.

capabilities.title: Durable subscriptions
capabilities.text: A subscription name and client ID keep copies while the consumer is offline; a new topic or selector replaces it.

capabilities.title: JMS selectors
capabilities.text: The SQL-92 subset on headers and properties: IN, LIKE, BETWEEN, IS NULL, arithmetic. A bad one gets InvalidSelectorException.

capabilities.title: Scheduler
capabilities.text: AMQ_SCHEDULED_DELAY, PERIOD with REPEAT, and CRON on the environment's clock; BROWSE and REMOVE over JMS work too.

capabilities.title: Dead letters as ActiveMQ does
capabilities.text: Poisoned, past max_redeliveries or expired persistent messages go to ActiveMQ.DLQ, or one DLQ per destination.

capabilities.title: Consumers like a real broker
capabilities.text: Prefetch, pull, ack modes, browsers, noLocal, exclusive and priority consumers, wildcards and message groups.

capabilities.title: Advisories
capabilities.text: Connection, consumer, producer, destination, expired and DLQ advisories with the real payloads, while someone listens.

capabilities.title: Wire format as asked
capabilities.text: Loose or tight encoding, with or without the marshal cache, compressed bodies and blob messages.

callouts.title: Counts by state
callouts.text: Scheduled, pending, delivered, acked, dead-letter and expired for the destination.

callouts.title: Scheduled by cron
callouts.text: AMQ_SCHEDULED_CRON on the environment clock; advance_clock brings it forward.

callouts.title: Inside a transaction
callouts.text: Delivered in a transaction that is still open: the ack takes effect only on commit.

callouts.title: Redelivery count
callouts.text: Redelivered 7 times, past max_redeliveries: the message went to the DLQ.

callouts.title: Moved to ActiveMQ.DLQ
callouts.text: The original keeps its state and points at its copy in the dead-letter queue.

excerpts.title: Send as the partner, then break the broker

callouts.title: Send a message
callouts.text: Text, properties and correlation id, dispatched to the app's consumers as the partner would.

callouts.title: Refuse login
callouts.text: Every login fails with a SecurityException.

callouts.title: Redeliver next 2
callouts.text: The next 2 acks are lost; those messages come again with a higher redelivery count.

callouts.title: Fail next commit
callouts.text: The commit fails with TransactionRolledBackException, or an XAException for XA.

callouts.title: Users
callouts.text: User names and passwords; empty lets anyone log in.

callouts.title: Selector
callouts.text: The consumer only gets messages whose properties match region = 'north'.

callouts.title: Wire format
callouts.text: What the client negotiated: tight encoding with the marshal cache, or loose.

callouts.title: Kept while offline
callouts.text: A durable subscription holds 12 messages until its client comes back.

callouts.title: Prepared XA
callouts.text: Phase one done; recover lists it from any connection until commit or rollback.

callouts.title: Committed
callouts.text: Local transactions with their sends and acks.

provoke.name: Login refused
provoke.what: Every login fails with a SecurityException

provoke.name: Connection dropped
provoke.what: The broker closes the connection after N dispatched messages

provoke.name: Lost acks
provoke.what: The next N acks are lost; those messages come again

provoke.name: Commit fails
provoke.what: The next N commits fail and roll back (XAException for XA)

provoke.name: Fast dead-lettering
provoke.what: Messages go to the DLQ after fewer redeliveries

provoke.name: Expired message
provoke.what: JMSExpiration passes; persistent ones go to the DLQ

provoke.name: Scheduled job cancelled
provoke.what: A delayed, repeating or cron message never goes out

advantages.title: No broker to run
advantages.text: No JVM, no activemq.xml: the app connects to 61616 and gets OpenWire 10 as NMS and the Java client expect.

advantages.title: See every message's state
advantages.text: Pending, delivered, in a transaction, rolled back or dead-lettered, which the web console never shows in one place.

advantages.title: Failures in the middle
advantages.text: A failed commit, a lost ack or a dropped connection after N messages, exactly where retries break.

advantages.title: Time you control
advantages.text: Scheduled, cron and expiring messages follow the environment clock, so a nightly job runs in a second.

agent.prompt: Check that our position consumer rolls back cleanly when a commit fails.
steps: the next commit fails with TransactionRolledBackException
seq 51 acked on attempt 2: one rollback, redelivered, then committed
tools: Queues, topics, consumers, durable subscriptions, transactions
Messages newest first, with their state
Send as the partner: properties, priority, delay, ttl, cron
Users and broker behaviour: refuse, drop, redeliver, fail commits
Cancel scheduled messages before they go out
Move the environment's clock: scheduled and expiring messages follow

notes: One port serves every environment: the default one answers.
Not made: network-of-brokers and memory-limit advisories (TempQueue, SlowConsumer, FULL).
